doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

chapter: Big bands in the Bay Area
title: Wartime dance-band boom: Hampton and Cab Calloway at Oakland Auditorium
summary: The Navy band is rated top in the Twelfth Naval District; Oakland draws huge crowds for Hampton and Calloway.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well they had bands all over the place you know. So they picked our band. Now I don’t know why. I found out in later years that the Captain of our station, he was somehow related to somebody, one of the Admirals here in the Twelfth Naval District so I don’t know whether he had the pull or what, but then of course we always met the challenge. Every week we’d have at least three tunes. And special arrangements. And also at that time during the war this area was one of the greatest areas for dance bands. That Oakland auditorium, Lionel Hampton used to pull seven thousand people, seventy-five hundred people. One of the times in the forties when Cab Calloway came out to do a picture, I think it was “Cabin in the Sky,” but he came up to our Golden Gate Theater to see the band, just to do the Golden Gate Theater truly they had Vaudeville and they featured name bands. But this has to do with Cab Calloway and the dance, the fact that of showing how this area was such a marvelous draw for dancers. Cab Calloway did the theater and then he played the Oakland auditorium. They had ten thousand people and the fire department closed the doors. And the people were milling around outside. I was one of them. And somebody opened the side door and I slipped in.
